Description: python Ark/tools/session_bench.py measures the real client in full screen on a fixed camera path (a turn at the start, then a flight over the terrain), one launch per setup: every frame time, graphics card and thread load, how far creatures were drawn, and proof that the window was in front; --profile adds a Flight Recorder file that java Ark/tools/SessionProfile.java breaks down by mod and method. Setups switch parts off (full, noshader, nograss, nodh, taau75, taau50, bare, nomobs, barenomobs), set the real render distance with fog around it (rd6 to rd16), another garbage collector (zgc, shenandoah, g1short), fewer Distant Horizons threads (dh2, dh3, dh3taau75) or an older creature path (serializer, easing; --draw, F27), and --repeat N --interleave runs them in turn. --prepare --biome minecraft:plains --pregen 128 makes the world (started in the middle of the nearest plains, 128 chunks around it generated by Chunky, 1 h 25 min on this machine), and --path return [--record] [--config section.key=value] flies out and back over it instead: a minute at a place 768 blocks from the start, a flight until it is beyond the loaded land, 150 s away and the return, each a phase of the table, with the session recorder running (B07, C05).

Description: One population budget places Ark wildlife (no vanilla spawn list). A chunk gets its share of animals once, when it is first loaded (plant eaters first and only what the land feeds), only where no player has them in plain sight (populationOutOfSight), and a region short of its quota takes arrivals in over days (populationRefillDays), as records anywhere in the land seen of it; nothing is removed, the first rules, LEDGER and BUDGET stay for comparison, /arkwildlife land prints a region with its food and pressures, and the rules are in Ark/README.md, Spawn rules.

Item: Wildlife that lasts: every creature traced from its appearance to its death
Description: Every wild animal is on a saved register (feature/spawn/WildlifeRegister) from the moment it joins the world until an end on record (the day, the place and the cause of its death, a taming or a removal); one the server has sent to a client is never deleted and no creature despawns the vanilla way. As a chunk loads its animals are where and as their records are and a record born or arrived meanwhile gets its body; silentRules = ODDS brings back the first rules, and spawning.wildCalendarSpeed runs the register's calendar faster than the sun for validation (Ark/README.md, Spawn rules).

Description: python Ark/tools/session_inspect.py <then> <now> --bench <folder> --bench <folder> reads recordings of the wildlife register (B07) and writes Ark/design/existence/inspector.html, one file apart from the game and the showcase, for validation: prey and predators day by day with bodies and records apart, the band of the existence model (F33) lived on from the very animals of the recording wherever a region had none of them in the world, predators against prey, the pressures, entries and ends by cause, every animal's life as a line, the cost second by second and a now-and-then table of two runs. Eight checks say what a run has to show (every record accounted for, none dropped for want of room, the land left alone bounded and every class alive in it, inside the model's band, pressure at or below the land, hunted as the pressures say, the place left persisted). Each run is entered in the ledger Ark/design/existence/runs.json (build, rules, population, rates per 100 animal-days, pressures, frames, server tick, budget pass), so population and performance can be followed from one build to the next.
Status:
Implemented; six runs are in the ledger, the last two a pair flown under the first and the bounded rules (C05). Looked at in a headless browser at 1320 px dark and 520 px light.
2026-10-08 (Claude Opus 5.5): the tool, the page and the ledger added; the bounded run holds all eight checks, the first rules fail 'every class alive' (the hunters of the land left alone were gone by day 60).
Open: the model's band exists only for the days a region has no body in the world (44 days for 13 regions on this flight; a flight away from the start would leave them alone longer); frame rates come from one run each, and the second of two runs starts with a warmer card; the page holds the two runs it was built for, the ledger the summaries of all; the selectors and the tooltips were not exercised in the headless browser.

Description: Looking at a creature within 24 blocks shows a small plate under the crosshair: its name and level, a health bar, and a tame's order (following, staying, wandering, working) or that it is unconscious. It is edged green for a tame, red for a wild hunter and tan for the rest, and fades half a second after the look moves off. Client setting creatureInfo hides it (client/CreatureInfoHud).
Status:
Implemented; unverified in client (compiled, data regenerated).
Open: for the user: the place under the crosshair and the 24-block reach are first choices; wild taming progress is not shown (the client does not have it).

Description: The inventory has no 2x2 grid: the Ark inventory (F38) draws the inventory's own workstation graph in its top band beside the worn gear, and its corner button opens the same graph full size, a menu carried by the player (design/workstations/inventory.json). It makes the field crafts (sharp rock, stone hatchet, flint knife, fire starter, fiber bandages, planks and the Working Station) and, under Bench work, the 69 small grid recipes of the benches without a screen (Bronze Blend, nuggets, books, unpacked blocks, sandstone, waxed copper, mushroom stew) at their future bench's level.

Description: The showcase's Recipes page fills the screen with a map of the 71 things the age makes, icons without names, held still at any zoom (it scrolls only when even its smallest icons do not fit): a row per station, a column per step from bare hands (one past the deepest input, held tool or needed station, worked out from the recipes, not a hand-made order). Hovering an item names it, gives its recipe, rate and what it goes into, and lights the chain it needs; python Ark/tools/recipe_tree.py checks that every input is gathered or made in the age and that nothing needs itself.
Status:
Implemented; looked at in headless Edge from 1150x600 to 1900x950 (fits without flicker, scrolls only below the smallest icons).

Open: the Bronze and Iron ages are not drawn yet; accessories, troughs and building blocks are left out of the map; the Hearty Stew's carrot only comes from villages.

Description: Every Prehistoric recipe asks for Ark-like amounts past the nine slots of a grid: bulk materials (fiber, twigs, logs, planks, cobblestone, clay) in tens, rocks and hide sparingly; a hatchet is 2 rocks, 3 twigs and 8 fiber, the Armoury 6 logs, 16 planks, 6 rocks and 12 fiber, the Primitive Forge a Stone Fire, 40 cobblestone, 16 clay and 3 hide. String and feathers left the early gear (bow, arrows, fishing rod, fiber bandage), 5 Narcoberries grind 2 Narcotics and 2 Narcotics tip 4 tranquilizer arrows, and the hide horse armour left the Armoury (horses are removed).
Status:
Implemented; unverified in client (pacing).
Open: troughs, accessories and saddles keep their old costs; whether loose rocks (2-5 a chunk, about 40 an age) and hide (0-5 a kill) are enough is for play to tell.

Description: The inventory key opens the Ark inventory in survival and adventure (creative keeps its own): a T-shaped panel in P16 carved stone, 336 x 228, whose top band holds the armour, offhand and 16 Curios slots in seven rows beside the player's arched niche and the crafting graph (F36), over a narrower block of storage eleven columns wide and the hotbar, its bottom corners cut away round carved consoles. The two added columns are six side pockets (a player attachment): pickups and crafts the full inventory cannot take go into them, crafts pay from them, they weigh, and they drop on death unless the inventory is kept.

Description: The showcase's Control page lists every recipe in the game: 1515 vanilla, 181 Ark (66 written only in a bench design, the 41 saddles among them) and the 32 of the pack's mods (Tom's Storage, FTB Quests), each with its fate (go, stay, change, decide), bench and note; a change gets its new cost and count in an editor under its row, and Incomplete lists kept recipes on no bench and changes without a cost. Description: Twenty-six species (Mammoth, Megapithecus, Sabertooth, Ankylosaurus, Tyrannosaurus, Triceratops, Direwolf, Parasaur, Velociraptor, Spinosaurus, Allosaurus, Carnotaurus, Giganotosaur, Ceratosaurus, Acrocanthosaurus, Dilophosaur, Terror Bird, Therizinosaurus, Pegomastax, Lystrosaurus and the swamp's Sarco, Kaprosuchus, Deinosuchus and Titanoboa and the sea's Megalodon, Mosasaurus and Plesiosaur) are designed box by box on their unchanged ARK rigs and clips, fitted to the original meshes' outlines and cross-sections, with skins painted texel by texel in each of their colour variants and their signature parts built, not painted: tusks and trunk, sabers, the ankylosaur's spikes and club, the trike's frill and horns, cut-out fur locks, crests, ridges, quills, feathers and the spino's sail, the allosaur's blade horns and paired scutes, the carno's swept horns and flank bosses, the giga's spike row, the cerato's nose horn and spiked tail, the acro's ridge and nape spines, the dilo's crests, feathers painted feather by feather on the terror bird and the therizinosaur with its scythe claws, the pegomastax's bristles, the lystrosaur's beak and tusks, the crocodiles' osteoderm rows, tail crests and interlocking cut-out teeth (the sarco's rosette, the kapro's fangs and horns, the deino's broad jaws), the titanoboa's forked tongue, the dilo's and the titanoboa's frills as one membrane on their ribs (a card per rib bone trimmed to its sector of the fan, filled when spread, folding with the clips) painted as a threat display with a false eye on each side, black band and serrated rim, cut-out rows of teeth; at sea fins, paddles, flippers and scute spikes traced from the ARK mesh's own triangles as cut-out cards on their own bones (handmade_models.sheet), rows of teeth standing outside shut mouths over dark gums, the megalodon's gill slits and rake scars.sheet), rows of teeth standing outside shut mouths over dark gums, the megalodon's gill slits and rake scars.sheet), its rows of serrated teeth standing out of the shut mouth over dark gums, gill slits and rake scars. Jaws are shaped shut as the idle holds them (the giga's, the sarco's and the kapro's, which their idles leave a little open, shut against the ARK mesh). Built by python scripts/handmade_models.py (also the Blockbench projects and previews); Creatures/Textures.py skips them and scripts/workflow.py rebuilds them after a refit.
Status:
Implemented; unverified in client.
2026-10-24 (Claude Opus 5.5): the Megalodon (141 boxes, was 103 fitted), Mosasaurus (137, was 126) and Plesiosaur (95, was 163) hand-made, checked against the ARK outlines and in idle, swim, bite and eye renders; no coplanar faces; verify_assets passes.
